description:
**File**: `src/services/app_state_service.cr:43-58`

**Severity**: P2 (mutex contention + GC pressure)

`AppStateService.update` runs `track_memory_usage` inside
`@mutex.synchronize`. `track_memory_usage` calls
`MemoryManagerActor.instance.get_memory_status`, which is a
`def_call` — every call allocates a `Channel(String).new(1)`, a
`CallGetMemoryStatus` struct, and round-trips a JSON reply (see
`infrastructure/actor.cr:_actor_call_with_timeout_json`).

The mutex is held across this round-trip, so every concurrent
state update (every refresh cycle, every websocket update) blocks
behind every other update's actor call. For a system that
updates state every few seconds, this serializes the slow path.

**Fix sketch**:
1. Snapshot `@current` into a local before releasing the mutex
2. Run `track_memory_usage` outside the mutex
3. Acquire the mutex only briefly to push the history entry

The throttling (every 10 updates) already limits this, but the
mutex-held region is still wider than necessary.

Found during code review 2026-06-18, see
`planning/code-review-2026-06-18.md` §5.1.
title: AppStateService.update holds @mutex across actor call (track_memory_usage)
